instruction_summary: Re-estimate Blanchard & Katz (1992) 'Regional Evolutions' main claims (C1-C4) on state panels extended through 2025, reusing the replication's VAR/IRF code, and show how each finding evolved from the original sample to now (rolling windows + named eras, COVID handling, state-cluster bootstrap bands).

steps.description: Read replication artifacts (log, code, results) and confirmed the ported VAR/IRF engines and that already-downloaded FRED raw CSVs span through mid-2026
Downloaded missing series: state participation LBSSA{FIPS} (x51) + national SA counterparts CE16OV, CLF16OV, CIVPART, UNRATE, PAYEMS from FRED public CSV endpoint
Built the extended annual panel 1939-2025 (51 units) with the instruction's exact household/relative-variable definitions; no SIC/NAICS splice needed ({ST}NAN continuous 1939-2025)
Ran the original-sample sanity gate: C1a 0.71/R2.758, C1b 1.63/1.53, C3 hh ur_yr1 0.37 & migration 0.383, C4a trough -0.83%; all pass except C2 yr5=0.08 (matches replication, LAUS-window feature)
Ran the full rolling-window + named-era sweep with 200-rep state-cluster bootstrap for C1-C4 (+ C3 COVID-dummied variant and payroll robustness)
Generated the 2x2 flagship figure and the supporting figure

key_results.C3_UR_halflife_all_windows: 3-4 years (transitory margins still die out fast)
key_results.C3_emp_year10_response_recent: toward 0 (V-shaped COVID recovery; less permanent recently)

comparison_to_original.note: reproduces; but slope fades to 0.37 for the newest 1990-2007->2007-2025 generation

comparison_to_original.quantity: C1b AR(4) employment level IR at year 4 / year 20
comparison_to_original.note: employment-shock permanence holds throughout the sweep

comparison_to_original.quantity: C2 AR(2) relative-UR IR at year 5 / year 10
comparison_to_original.note: year-10 ~0 in all windows; year-5 gate low vs paper 0.29, a LAUS short-window feature matching the replication

comparison_to_original.quantity: C3 year-1 out-migration share of adjustment
comparison_to_original.note: migration's share of adjustment fell ~1/3 on household basis; matches Dao-Furceri-Loungani (2017)

comparison_to_original.quantity: C4a income (PCPI) trough after -1% employment shock
comparison_to_original.note: income responds at least as much as originally; always transitory

deviations: No SIC->NAICS splice: FRED {ST}NAN is a continuous 1939-2025 state total-nonfarm series, so C1's long window uses one series (splice_ratios.csv ratio=1.0). Avoids the download.bls.gov 403 path; no effect on C1 (Fig-1 slope reproduces 0.70).

C2 year-5 IR gate lands at 0.08 (vs target [0.15,0.45]); reproduces the replication's 0.08 exactly, attributable to LAUS starting only in 1976 and revised/smoother LAUS data. Qualitative claim (year-10 ~0) unaffected.

C3 baseline uses household (LAUS) employment (migration benchmark 0.40) as instructed; the household year-1 UR response (0.37 pp) and shallower year-10 employment (-0.79%) differ in level from the paper's establishment-basis printed 0.32 pp / -1.3% by design (fn 37). Payroll robustness rows reproduce the deeper establishment plateau.
Optional C4b house-price VAR not run (conserved scope after all four required claims and mandatory outputs were complete).

Out of scope as in the replication: composition-adjusted CPS wage, manufacturing production-worker AHE (per-capita income used as the wage-side proxy, per the paper's Fig 13), pre-1976 state unemployment, and the defense-contract Bartik IV.
